first_impression.reaction: Fine, someone admits the other lists are recycled and promises sources. That's the right pitch for me. I skipped down to the FAQ and the Standesamt bit first, because the legal side is the only part where a mistake actually costs money.

journey.quote: Where a story is only "often told", we say so.
journey.reaction: Good. Saying up front what you're not sure of is exactly what I want to see.

journey.quote: Each custom is grouped by when it happens, from the week before to the morning after, and each meaning comes from a German heritage body, a German government page or a named editorial source.
journey.reaction: Big promise. Then plenty of later sections never tell me where they got it. The rings, the veil dance, the midnight cake and the 100-guest figure all come with no name attached. Only some lines say who the source is (The Local, BR, the Bavarian heritage wiki, Hannover). If you promise every meaning is sourced, show me the source in every section, or I start wondering which ones are padding.

journey.quote: German weddings also tend to be smaller, often around 100 guests or fewer.
journey.reaction: Says who? This is a number, and a number with no source is the kind of thing I check elsewhere.

journey.quote: Its age is often told as pre-Christian, but even the Bavarian heritage wiki that mentions this only says "probably" and offers no evidence.
journey.reaction: This line won me over more than anything else. You're telling me where your own source is weak.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, section 1310(1) of the German Civil Code (BGB) says a marriage is concluded only when the couple declare before the registrar (Standesbeamter) that they wish to marry each other.
journey.reaction: A statute, a section number and a date. This is the useful part of the page for me.

journey.section: What an Australian couple should check
journey.quote: A fee applies, even if the application is refused or withdrawn, and processing time varies.
journey.reaction: Honest about the catch. I'd still like the amount or a link to where it's published, but at least it isn't hidden.

journey.section: Getting married in Germany from Australia
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements with the Standesamt in writing before you book.
journey.reaction: In writing is the right phrase. That's a concrete commitment rather than 'we take care of everything'.

journey.section: Getting married in Germany from Australia (CTA)
journey.quote: One person works in your time zone and plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, with the fee agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: A fee in writing is good. But 'payments' and 'vendors' is exactly where I ask: do you take a commission from the venue or suppliers on top of that fee? The page doesn't say.

journey.section: Saving cents for the bridal shoes
journey.quote: It makes a lovely story for a speech, even if the shoes are paid for by card.
journey.reaction: Bit fluffy, but it's a traditions article. Doesn't bother me much.

journey.quote: We found no source we would stand behind on Swiss wedding customs, so for a wedding in Switzerland, ask your venue and your families.
journey.reaction: Rare to see a wedding site admit a gap. More of this.

unanswered_questions: Do you take a commission or mark-up from venues or suppliers, on top of the fee agreed in writing?
What does the Wedded Advisor fee actually cover for a German wedding? Standesamt paperwork, translations, the Hochzeitslader booking?
Where do the unattributed claims come from (rings on the right hand, veil dance, midnight cake, around 100 guests)?
What is the exemption (Befreiung) fee, or where is it published?
Have you actually planned a wedding in Germany? Show me a real one with the actual budget.

turn_offs_found.quote: This is the part that matters most for an Australian couple.
turn_offs_found.why: Mild, and mostly earned, but I decide what matters most to me. It's fine because the facts after it hold up.

would_share_with: My fiancee, mainly for the Standesamt and CNI sections

cta_reaction.quote: If the paperwork is the part keeping you up at night, speak with a Wedded Advisor.
cta_reaction.why: It comes after real evidence, not before, and 'fee agreed in writing' is the right signal. I'd click once I know whether there are supplier commissions. Right now I'd more likely save the page and compare it with the other two planners.

top_3_changes: Keep the intro's promise: name the source in-text for every custom (rings, veil dance, cake, guest numbers), not only for some, because the reader can't see the citations.
Next to 'fee agreed in writing', add one line on whether Wedded Wonderland takes commissions or mark-ups from venues and suppliers (or link to the page that explains the fee model).
Give the Befreiung fee figure or link the official page where it's published, so 'a fee applies' isn't a dead end.

checks.check: Every point has an exact quote from the draft
No invented brand facts; missing info listed in unanswered_questions
[[VERIFY]] markers and HTML comments treated as invisible
Deferred business details and absence of prices not treated as must-fix

open_questions.question: Commission/mark-up transparency is Daniel's core objection but is a business detail the orchestrator marked as deferred. Treat it as a future fee-model page link rather than a must-fix for this post?

assumptions: Arrived from a Google search for 'german wedding traditions'; Daniel is planning a wedding with a German connection and comparing planners.
HTML fact comments are invisible to the reader, so claims without an in-text attribution read as unsourced.
